purpose: The sixteen-factor Top10 book earns roughly 7-14 bps gross per pick against a 30 bps round-trip cost assumption, so every weighting variant tested so far is net negative. Reweighting moves gross inside a band that never reaches the cost line. This module tests the axis nobody has varied: the holding horizon. The same round-trip cost is paid once regardless of how long the position is held, so the question is whether gross edge grows fast enough with horizon to clear a fixed cost, and whether the frozen weighting still matters once the horizon changes.
knownLimitations: A fixed 30 bps round-trip assumption is a modelling choice, not a measured fill; real A-share cost varies with size, liquidity and stamp duty and is not constant across the cross-section.
Longer horizons mechanically reduce the number of independent observations, so the day-clustered t at 20 sessions rests on far fewer effective samples than at 1 session.
Overlapping holding windows at horizons above one session induce autocorrelation that a simple day-clustered t does not fully absorb.
The best single factor is chosen after seeing the grid, so its apparent edge carries multiple-testing exposure; only the full distribution across factors is interpretable.
Every historical evaluation window has already been viewed, so this run can reject a horizon but can never validate or promote one.
Gross returns ignore borrow, price limits at the exit open and any impact beyond the cost assumption.
